implementationScope: Bounded native citation repairs. No external facts, identifier digits, source attribution or unsupported field is invented or deleted.

ids.limit: Missing first separator only before one explicit URL in an active literal Cite web call. Historical examples in HTML comments are deliberately untouched.
Only an explicit Fecha prefix followed by a complete calendar-valid named-month date; dates feature flags retained.
Identical same-key values only, with all duplicates equal; includes complete literal refs in known native infoboxes. Comments and conflicting last-value semantics are preserved.

Finite obsolete fields Título/publicado por/conferência-url. Conference URL uses accepted conference-url, because the proposed Portuguese-looking alternative is not whitelisted. Protected quotations are untouched.
Verified legacy music-notes helper only: year/Format/publisher restore existing values. No global reversal of Portuguese field names.
Bare upper-alpha collector or one complete named reference bank. Preserves group, bank bytes and labels; no custom widths/columns or embedded collectors.
Invalid access-key spelling with already-valid native enum; URL and archive-state safety required, literal enum retained.
Reuse existing date-key guards inside one complete literal ref owned by a known infobox or image. No arbitrary nested strings.
Reuse existing archive-pair/URL-state guards inside that same narrow native-reference ownership path.
Existing issue alias repair becomes reachable in a literal infobox footnote; edition, page and all values remain distinct.
Ordinary refs covered by the inherited uncertainty/quotation quarantine stay unchanged. No global bypass to force an original-year repair.
Finite compound paragraph locator only, in a full native citation, without another locator. Short-citation loc remains valid and untouched. Inherited uncertain contexts remain protected.
Article identifiers are not converted to pages. An opaque-locator interface or native support still requires a complete semantic contract.
At least two explicit Italian interface fields, native web target, all filled fields preservable, valid literal dates and matching archive target/date. Other interfaces are not guessed.
Anonymous external link becomes URL only when its label repeats the existing original title exactly after whitespace normalization.
Whole anonymous arxiv helper with the proved gr-qc archive and seven-digit ID, no competing ID. The same eprint target is retained.
One terminal dot on an otherwise valid ISBN; no check digit is recomputed.
Only identical valid ISBN repetitions inside one value; keeps the first literal spelling.
Exactly equivalent valid ISBN-10/978 ISBN-13 pair, no existing id. Both literal numbers and links remain; primary ISBN is structured COinS, secondary stays in an ISBN id helper.
Only U+200E at an ASCII HTTP URL boundary; no internal controls or non-ASCII URL changes. Complete literal refs in balanced native tables may use this repair without rewriting table tokens.
Missing archive date only, exact 8/14-digit Wayback capture and exactly matching source URL. All date aliases checked; publication/access dates and URL state remain unchanged.
Malformed scheme remains unchanged without independently proved intended destination.
Only a unique literal original title from compatible native web citations with the exact same specific URL and no conflicting metadata.
Pinned defective native CS1 dependency only; key-only vautores/veditores compatibility mapping, destination absent and all names preserved. Updated module contracts disable it.

controls: No new implementation of already-working editor-name, display-author, original-year, publication-date, page-total or PMC-prefix normalizations.
No bioRxiv addition here: that candidate is prior50 coverage, outside the 76-choice implementation scope.
No removal of meaningful values merely to eliminate a diagnostic.
Protected comments, nowiki, quotations, code, unknown wrappers, conflicting values and the known extreme timeout remain preserved.
